title: Safety and efficacy of micropulse in pediatric eyes with refractory glaucoma

license.statement: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (article <license>, ali:license_ref); non-commercial share-alike, therefore private

indication: pediatric (< 18 years) refractory glaucoma: primary congenital, juvenile, glaucoma after vitreoretinal surgery, after congenital cataract surgery and other secondary childhood glaucoma; 18 of 23 eyes had previous glaucoma interventions; hospital-based prospective interventional single-arm study (Southern India)

groups.description: micropulse transscleral cyclophotocoagulation (Iridex Cyclo G6, MP3 probe, 2000 mW, 31.33% duty cycle, 360 degrees for 160 s) under general anesthesia; 23 eyes of 23 patients

series.notes: mean ± SD (Methods: continuous variables presented as mean and SD; the W/T footnote marks the test of each comparison, not the summary statistic); follow-up cells also contain the comparison p-value in parentheses (not used); column header gives n=23 for all rows; 11 eyes received additional IOP-lowering interventions during follow-up (9 tubes, 2 repeat MP-TSCPC; 2 within 1 month, 6 between 1-3 months, 3 between 3-6 months) and the Results state the tabulated IOP reduction is not entirely attributable to MP-TSCPC, i.e. these eyes were not censored

exclusions.reason: measured but not tabulated (only plotted in Figure 1); figure values are not cited cells

exclusions.what: Figure 1 dotted line: eyes without additional IOP-lowering interventions
exclusions.reason: analysis set selected by a postoperative outcome (no additional intervention) and figure-only

exclusions.what: Table 2 p-values (in parentheses within the follow-up cells)

exclusions.reason: medication numbers are not IOP series in schema 1.0.0; noted only

exclusions.what: Table 3 complete/partial success, failure and additional-intervention counts; Figure 2 Kaplan-Meier
exclusions.reason: success proportions, counts and Kaplan-Meier estimates are not admissible

notes: Reference kind 'preoperative_medicated': patients were advised to continue the anti-glaucoma medications prescribed preoperatively, and the baseline number of IOP-lowering agents is tabulated (t2!R2C4); no washout described.
Tonometer: ICARE 200 rebound tonometer before and after the laser, without anesthesia or sedation, average of six readings (method 'rebound').
Inclusion required at least three follow-up visits within 6 months; exclusion of eyes with intraocular surgery or laser within 2 months before MP-TSCPC or any prior cyclophotocoagulation.
Single-arm study of a standard laser procedure without an investigational agent, so the group is 'control'.
Number of IOP-lowering agents at baseline and 1/3/6 months is tabulated in Table 2 (not extracted).
